evidence: Native launcher main at 0x401000 delegates to its archive extractor; 0x401484 parses the E0E0..E7E7 archive header; 0x40171f unmasks only the first 2000 engine bytes with XOR 7; 0x401b89 stages irsetup.exe in an _ir_sf_temp directory and 0x401e8a invokes it.

The recovered engine is stock-shaped Setup Factory 9.5.3.0, packed with ordinary UPX. Full decompression succeeds once its header masking is reproduced correctly. Launcher has no Authenticode signature; the embedded Lua DLL has Indigo Rose certificate material.

LZMA stream at 0x1b733e contains installer configuration and complete event scripts. It installs AlmofidDLL.dll and DataBase.accdb under C:\ALMOFID. Product, author, installation and uninstall events agree; custom install events are empty apart from standard reboot handling.

Recovered 37376-byte VB.NET DLL at LZMA offset 0x1ddf3b: AlmofidPass.AlmofidValidation is an integer lookup/switch and AlmofidValidationRotation uses character arithmetic. All methods and member references were examined via dnfile/dncil; no network, process-launch, payload-loading or credential collection call path is present.

The remaining large member starts with Standard ACE DB and Office encryption metadata. The updater copies the database; no execution of database content is configured. Encrypted database contents cannot be independently audited without its password.

Unpacked engine 0x4548ae resolves SRRemoveRestorePoint as a system-restore wrapper. This capability alone proves neither bulk removal nor sabotage. At 0x41ef84, the oledlg.dll missing diagnostic follows an actual failed LoadLibraryA of the system-directory DLL; it is a real dependency error. Cleanup includes a /c del command.

The supplied Triage report was fetched over HTTPS. Its score-10 custom signature is UPX dump on original entry point; other signatures are dropped EXE/DLL loading, UPX, locale/registry and device queries. Those observations fit the installer. The product homepage was fetched but DNS resolution failed.
samples.missing_context: No known deployment circumstances or live publisher distribution were available. The encrypted Access data remains opaque; this is a balance-of-evidence benign judgment, not a provenance allowlist.

evidence: 8722-byte artifact includes a zeroed 256-byte PSP prefix; its 8466-byte program starts at memory/file offset 0x100. PSP-stripped bytes are a conventional COM layout.

At 0x11c DX=0x21d5 addresses the embedded C:\COMMAND.COM path. XOR CX,CX followed by AX=3C02h and INT 21h creates/truncates it with normal attributes. AL=2 is ignored by this function; no hidden-attribute claim is justified.

At 0x136 AH=40h writes CX=0x2112 (8466) bytes from DS:0100 to the returned file handle, then AH=3Eh closes it. This replaces the DOS command interpreter with the self image and destroys its previous contents.

Repeated EB 01 90 sequences skip NOP bytes between saved registers and DOS operations. Subsequent INT 10h AX=1110h installs a 256-character custom font block; this is retained as a neutral display capability.
samples.coverage_gap: One distinct hostile behavior (interpreter infection/overwrite) and one suspicious obfuscation behavior are supported. A second hostile claim would duplicate the same overwrite or invent intent for ordinary BIOS font loading.
samples.classifier_gap: Atomscan v2.13.0 treats the artifact as unknown and emits no YAML findings. Cleave 3.0.0-beta.2 identifies dos_com and fires the new hostile overwrite, suspicious padding and notable file/font observations. This is an analyzer/classifier gap; no score-padding duplicates were added.

evidence: Go 1.23.1 GUI executable, module MeridianSphereAnalytics, randomized main identifiers and extensive byte-transform/junk loops. The intact SHA-256 Authenticode digest and verified timestamp do not establish publisher trust: the Meridian Sphere Analytics leaf is self-signed.

Statically traced main.main and all main-package helpers via Go objdump. Decoder main.usXydlc4Y3 at 0x55a320 reconstructs a 0x16097b-byte payload through multiple position-dependent subtraction, pair swap and XOR stages. Register variants previously escaped the existing arithmetic/reassembly matchers.

A Unicorn run of the actual Go code, with OS and runtime service stubs, recovered an import-free PE64 with image base 0x660000000 and entry RVA 0x2225c. The loader reserves RWX memory, maps sections, applies relocation processing and registers the exception table using RtlAddFunctionTable.

NtQueryInformationThread supplies a TEB pointer. main.bBjGsctjmt follows TEB+0x60 to the PEB, then stores the mapped payload base at PEB+0x10. Instrumented write at instruction 0x506edb wrote 0x30160b60 to the synthetic PEB ImageBaseAddress field. Main computes the same mapped base plus entry RVA and calls syscall.SyscallN at 0x4f0700; the stub logged activation target 0x30182dbc.

The native stage uses PEB/environment gating and hashed API resolution. Safe partial emulation resolved GetCommandLineA, GetModuleFileNameA, CreateFileA, ReadFile, CloseHandle and SetFilePointer; it did not establish credential theft or successful live execution. Its self-image header read could not be fully satisfied by the synthetic OS context.
samples.judgment_basis: Concealed native payload activation and PEB image identity substitution, combined with obfuscation, self-issued branding and malware-corpus provenance, tip the judgment. No legitimate product or authorized deployment context was established; the filename and signature are not treated as behavioral proof.

coverage_additions: DOS create/write/close sequence, DS:DX-bound COMMAND.COM create target, overwrite composite, skipped-NOP register-save padding, BIOS custom-font loading

Existing Go arithmetic, adjacent-pair swap, entry-field sum/call and pointer-chain store matchers retain old forms and accept observed register forms; existing unpacker and PEB-substitution composites now fire.
corrections: Moved srclient.dll reference from an impact objective to fs/path/library and SRRemoveRestorePoint reference to os/recovery. Moved native-restore-point-deletion to a notable native-restore-point-api-profile: its required evidence was API co-occurrence, not sabotage. Both raw-disk wiper consumers now reference the preserved neutral profile.

Moved fake-error-dll-missing to notable ui/dialog/error::missing-dll-diagnostic. The actual engine branch displays it only after a real missing dependency; text alone supplied no fake/lure evidence. No direct consumers required rewiring.

Moved COMSPEC short-path cleanup to notable fs/delete/file/self and named it a reference profile. Added required /c del text because module-path and shell APIs alone did not establish deletion. Removed a platform-signer downgrade below notable. Updated both exact consumers; the original engine still matches cleanup capability.
rule_changes.consumer_audit: Exact references and ancestor selectors were inspected. The generic impact/degrade selector in the native-filter backdoor is ELF-scoped, disjoint from the relocated Windows profile. CrystalX uses impact as a suppression; this broad false-positive impact signal no longer suppresses identity, and the installer has none of its required family legs.

retained_attack_fixture.result: All 21 findings identical against a git-archive HEAD baseline and the revised traits.

tests.byte_transform_bounds: 18 cases: original/new register forms, incorrect stores/offsets/sum and non-code controls
tests.native_loader_reasoned_review: 8 cases including real Go sample dependency removals; removing the image-base store retains unpacking but removes substitution; removing decoding or entry setup removes both hostile findings
tests.dos_command_overwrite: 5 cases: full PSP-bearing memory image, stripped COM, unrelated path despite retained COMMAND.COM text, missing write, and missing font operation

emitted_classifier_verdicts.disagreement: Both malicious samples still receive BENIGN; the Go sample is now covered by two hostile and two suspicious findings, while DOS remains unknown to Atomscan despite supported dos_com analysis in standalone Cleave. The benign updater retains a high probability. Do not add inaccurate traits to alter these decisions.

verification.cleanup_narrowing_control: An engine copy with /c del replaced by /c echo retains all API context. The old self-delete composite matches it; the new deletion-reference profile requires the actual delete command and does not match.

limitations: No samples were launched as native programs. Disassembly and controlled CPU emulation are static/isolated evidence, not live compromise observations.

Atomscan reports v18 feature-spec compatibility warnings against the v19 extractor. Numeric probabilities and the emitted decision fields are recorded separately; neither determines the analyst verdict.
